findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. A newcomer could repeat it after one read.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but the title and almost all of the page are about another project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets one paragraph on it and then a long technical study of a tool they may never have heard of.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title>; h1 "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The page does say why the study is there: it is a sample of Athena's work. But it never shows Athena's main product, a traced commit made from a short request, so the newcomer only gets a side capability as the example.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim"

findings.text: The next step is easy to find and concrete: a repo link, a clone command, the prerequisites, `./setup.sh`, and an example `athena ask "add a changelog"`. This is the page's strongest part for a newcomer.
findings.source: Header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself"; section "Next steps"

findings.text: The page does not say which repository the command acts on, whether it commits straight away, or what accounts and costs are needed beyond Claude Code. A careful newcomer would want those answered before pressing Enter.
findings.source: Next steps: "have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm"; "press Enter to run it on your repository"

findings.text: This link is aimed at the project's owner, but it sits in the header next to the newcomer's next step. A first-time visitor has no proposals waiting and won't know what it means.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The firstmate study is careful and every statement is cited, but it is long and full of jargon ("exit 75", "places-held", "close-pending", "mode=retain"). A newcomer will likely skim or leave before reaching the Next steps section at the bottom.
findings.source: Sections "Transitions" (cards t1–t12), "Counters", "Glossary" (about 40 terms), "Claims and sources" (45 claims)

findings.text: A newcomer who does read on gets a clear one-sentence definition of firstmate. The "Words used first" list also defines terms before they are used, which helps.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker"

findings.text: Some text describes Athena's own internal workings (study folders, the first reading that missed paths). That means nothing to a newcomer and adds length without helping them decide what to do.
findings.source: Section "About this page": "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"; Limits f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths"
